requirement:
The requirements index links to its documented-coverage-gaps subchapter
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index`.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.test-coverage.index.navigation` says only that "The requirements index links to its documented-coverage-gaps subchapter under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index`." This describes observable output: the generated requirements index contains a link to that subchapter.

I checked the clause for structural obligations. It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or named interface that the implementation must use.

I also tried an alternative implementation that gives the same observable result. It builds the link through a different internal mechanism, such as a different helper function, data structure or generation order. The generated index would still link to the subchapter, so the clause would still be met. How the link gets into the index is therefore discretionary.

The cited `requirements.test-coverage.index` supplies context only. It says `habeas mdbook` generates the subchapter. That is its own behavioral obligation, and it is not delegated to this requirement.

No implementation roots are supplied, and none are needed. Tests supply the evidence for the link, so there is nothing to mark `{impl}`. No acknowledgments are present.

behavioral: The requirement has one observable obligation. The requirements index must link to its documented-coverage-gaps subchapter, which sits under that index. The parent requirement `requirements.test-coverage.index` says this applies whether the index is explicitly placed or automatically generated. I did not read the implementation. Three marked tests cover the obligation.

- `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` covers an explicitly placed `{requirements-index}` chapter. It asserts these things:
  - Exactly one "Documented coverage gaps" chapter is among the index's sub_items.
  - Its path is `appendix/requirements-index/coverage.md`.
  - Its parent_names are `["Requirements index"]`.
  - The index content contains `[Documented coverage gaps](requirements-index/coverage.html)`.
- `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` covers the automatically generated default index. It makes the same assertions: one coverage subchapter, path `requirements-index/coverage.md`, parent `Requirements index`, and the link in the index content. It also checks that the coverage chapter is kept apart from the detail pages.
- `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` covers a nested index, both with and without section numbers. It asserts the parent content contains `[Documented coverage gaps](reports/coverage.html)`. It also asserts that the coverage chapter's path, parent_names and number place it under the index.

Together these cover the placed and generated index cases, top-level and nested placement, and both the link and the subchapter's position. A regression that dropped the link, pointed it at the wrong path, or put the chapter elsewhere would fail these assertions. I found no unaddressed obligation.
